expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Full DocumentsTable component with state management, API helpers, and all UI components

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: Complete runnable React component with full hook implementation and event handlers

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Undo available only for archive: 'if (action === "archive" && result.undoExpiresAt)'. Delete requires typing confirmation but has no recovery: 'await postJson(.../delete...); setSelection(emptySelection()); setDeleteOpen(false)' with no undo mechanism

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: DeleteDialog displays 'Permanently delete {documentLabel(count)}?' and requires typing 'DELETE ${count.toLocaleString()} DOCUMENTS'

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Selection discriminated: kind 'ids' vs 'allMatching'. Explicit selectAllMatching() function and separate UI for each state

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive: bg-white with ring-1 (outlined). Delete: bg-red-600 (filled red). Clear visual distinction

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: Delete button has no autoFocus. DeleteDialog autofocuses the text input, not the delete button

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: 'the bulk endpoints enforce authorization, scope validity, soft-archive undo, and idempotency server-side'

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Closing discusses mechanisms (idempotency, locking, scope binding) and constraints (page selection limits) but does not explicitly enumerate prevented misuse scenarios
